note: The machine-readable form of spec/SPEC.md section 10.1. Same content, different reader: a human applies the table, a loader applies this. Ruled 2026-08-08 (S-17). A reader that does not support a declared convention looks it up here, refuses exactly the node types in `governs` with report code unsupported-convention, and loads, lists, hash-verifies and extracts everything else. The graph listing, the hashes and the work notes are readable knowledge that no convention gates. Stage 12 added core.geom.points and core.geom.gsplat to the envelope-binary rows and two OPTIONAL conventions, sh_coeff_order and sh_degree; an entry carrying "optional": true is a convention a manifest may omit, and a reader that meets its absence uses the profile default stated in SPEC.md rather than reporting a missing convention. The 2026-10-13 entries (PROPOSED) add core.scene, the versioned record of part placement and display (SPEC.md section 3.20), to the length, axis and quaternion rows: its transforms are the same TRS, in the same units and the same quaternion order, as parts[] in the manifest.

endianness.note: Every envelope binary. core.skeleton only through its optional binary mirror; the JSON skeleton has no endianness.

alignment_bytes.note: The same set as endianness: payload sections in envelope binaries start on this boundary.

units_per_meter.note: core.anim.clip through its root translation and any bone-translation section; core.retarget.bind through the solved stature scale; core.imposter through the depth range; core.props through any length-valued property.

angle_unit.note: core.skeleton through joint limits; core.retarget.bind through residuals and tolerances; core.props through any angle-valued property.

up_axis.note: Every node carrying a direction or a position in model space. For core.retarget.bind the solved basis rotation is source-to-THESE axes, so refusing them makes the bind meaningless rather than merely unusable.

quat_order.note: The one convention whose reach extends outside nodes[]: part placement in the manifest itself is quaternions too, and no node-type list can say so. core.geom.gsplat carries one quaternion per Gaussian in its `rotations` stream and its envelope header restates the order, because the PLY it was ingested from does NOT declare one (spec/layouts/gsplat.layout.txt section 6).

oct_encoding_pole.note: core.imposter through its octahedral normal channel; any x.* using octahedral encoding.

sh_l1_order.note: No core node uses it today. It is declared because x.cub.* and any other extension carrying L1 spherical harmonics needs it pinned, and a convention agreed on only once an extension arrives is a convention nobody agreed on.

color_space_default.note: core.semantics through the palette. Only where the node does not declare its own color_space, which every conformant core.tex does and which a core.geom.points field with semantic 'color' is likewise required to do.

uv_origin.note: core.geom.* through TEXCOORD_*; core.material through texture slots.

text_encoding.note: Every text and JSON payload in the package, INCLUDING MANIFEST.json — which is why the scope is container: a reader that cannot do UTF-8 cannot read the manifest at all.

id_case.note: Every id in the manifest and in every payload.

hash_algorithm.note: Every files[].sha256, every input_hash, license.sha256, and spec_sha256.

signature_algorithm.note: SIGNATURE.json only. Refusing it is the 'unverified' state of SPEC.md section 10 step 4 — a fourth fixed token meaning 'I did not check' — and it is not damage.

sh_coeff_order.note: Added Stage 12. Memory order of a per-primitive spherical-harmonic coefficient array. OPTIONAL in the manifest: absence means 'coefficient-major', which spec/layouts/gsplat.layout.txt section 4 requires anyway, so every package written before this key existed is unaffected. It is NOT sh_l1_order — that names the BASIS order an x.* extension uses for per-vertex L1 irradiance, this names a memory order, and collapsing them would give one convention two meanings (D-GS-3).

sh_degree.note: Added Stage 12, and ADVISORY even where it governs: a package-level MAXIMUM so a store can size a buffer before parsing, never the authority on a payload. Each WKGS envelope declares its own sh_degree and that governs that payload. A payload declaring more than the manifest is a producer error a reader REPORTS (sh-degree-exceeds-declared) rather than resolving. Refusing this convention is therefore never grounds to refuse a node.
